rv.q: I've written more than once in this space about the flaws of 'Angels.' It's too long, too sentimental, too inclined to demonize at the expense of comprehension, too rigid in its Marx-flavored politics ('Angels' would be a richer play if Mr. Kushner had had the wit, not to mention the honesty, to portray Ethel Rosenberg as shamelessly guilty).
But the reason it persists, the reason companies will stage this work for decades to come, is that it's first and foremost great, riveting drama.
